headline: Chevron in talks with US on wider Venezuela oil license, sources say
summary: STORY: The U.S. government may allow oil giant Chevron to increase its crude exports from Venezuela.That's according to four sources who told Reuters the two are in talks about expanding a license the company has to operate in the South American country.The change would allow Chevron to boost exports to its own refineries and sell oil to other buyers.The talks come as Washington and Caracas continue discussions about supplying up to 50 million barrels of Venezuelan oil to the United States ... and as President Donald Trump presses American oil companies to invest in Venezuela's energy sector.U.S. officials have said this week that proceeds from the Venezuelan oil supply will go to a U.S.-overseen trustee. Proceeds are meant to finance supplies of American goods to Venezuela.Chevron is the only U.S. oil major operating in Venezuela, which it does under an authorization from the U.S. government that exempts it from sanctions on the country.As part of its sanction-hardening campaign to weaken Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro, the Trump administration in July put additional restrictions on Chevron's license. Those restrictions reduced the volume of Venezuelan crude the company is exporting to the U.S. by 60%.The restrictions also deprived Venezuelan state-run oil company PDVSA of any proceeds from Chevron's exports.The license expansion would allow Chevron to go back to previous export levels while providing Venezuelan crude to business partners that could allocate the oil to destinations other than the U.S., as the company used to do in the past.Sources said Washington is also pushing to have other U.S. companies involved in oil exports from Venezuela, including refiner Valero Energy, which was a customer of Venezuela's PDVSA before the sanctions.The U.S. is also pushing to get oil majors Exxon Mobil and ConocoPhillips involved as well. Their Venezuelan assets were expropriated two decades ago.Chevron, Valero, Exxon and Conoco did not immediately reply to requests for comment.

summary: STORY: Donald Trump's administration is planning to meet with executives from U.S. oil companies later this week.That's according to a Reuters source, who says the meetings are to discuss boosting Venezuelan oil production after U.S. forces ousted country leader Nicolas Maduro.The administration is eyeing getting U.S. oil companies back into the South American nation, after its government took control of U.S.-led energy operations there nearly two decades ago. The White House did not comment on the planned meetings.But said it believed U.S. industry was ready to move into Venezuela.The three biggest U.S. oil companies - Exxon Mobil, ConocoPhillips and Chevron - did not immediately respond to requests for comment.According to four industry executives, the three firms have not yet had any conversations with the administration about Maduro's ouster.That contradicts Trump's statements over the weekend.The president said he had already held meetings with all the U.S. oil companies, both before and after Maduro was seized.Trump also said that he expects the firms to spend billions of dollars to boost Venezuela's oil production.But industry analysts say those plans will face challenges.They cite lack of infrastructure, and deep uncertainty over the country’s political future and legal framework, as well as doubts over long-term U.S. policy.

headline: Trump Tells Oil Giants to “Get Ready” for a Post-Maduro Venezuela
summary: President Donald Trump is pressing U.S. oil majors to prepare for large-scale investment in Venezuela following the capture of Nicolás Maduro, though industry enthusiasm remains uncertain given the scale, cost, and risks involved.
